source.title: An Investigation into Neural Net Optimization via Hessian Eigenvalue Density
source.authors: B. Ghorbani; Shankar Krishnan; Ying Xiao

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation affecting the extracted findings.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures optimization behavior and training speed alongside Hessian spectra, including BN ablations and a BN-statistics intervention. These results bear on V6, but do not test training classification error as described by the overall claim.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study's own BN-related training-speed results and its measured Hessian and gradient outcomes that bear on V6. The authors' citations about BN training speed are not extracted as results. Validation accuracy and unrelated spectrum-estimation validation results are omitted.
record.test_reason: The population-statistics intervention directly measures optimization speed and reports learning-rate restrictions, bearing on V6's dependence on the normalization procedure. Hessian and gradient spectra alone do not measure any version's stated effect.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' interpretation, but should preserve its status as a proposed mechanism: they argue that BN suppresses relative Hessian outliers and associated gradient concentration, thereby accelerating optimization. The population-statistics intervention supports this explanation, while showing that the largest eigenvalue alone cannot explain speed.
record.recipe_differences: This paper studies Hessian and gradient spectra and selected optimization-speed comparisons; it does not reproduce the claim's training-error measurements or the BN speed comparisons named in V6.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch-normalization presence changes Hessian and gradient outlier behavior. Replacing mini-batch BN statistics with population statistics yields slower training and persistent outliers, although the largest Hessian eigenvalue remains roughly the same.

fits_no_version.finding: BN suppresses relative Hessian outliers and reduces concentration of gradient energy in dominant eigenspaces.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mini-batch BN changes Hessian and gradient geometry relative to networks without BN.

fits_no_version.finding: Population-statistics and mini-batch BN have roughly equal largest Hessian eigenvalues despite substantially different optimization speeds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The largest Hessian eigenvalue alone is insufficient to explain optimization speed.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing residual connections contracts the ResNet-32 Hessian spectrum toward zero at step 40000.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual connections need not reduce local Hessian curvature; this does not test depth-related training-error degradation.

fits_no_version.finding: The Hessian spectrum contracts after the learning-rate drop at step 40000.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Lower learning rates need not produce sharper local curvature; no stability-threshold recovery is measured.

record.problems: Training-speed comparisons are largely qualitative in the supplied text; the spectrum comparisons are primarily figures without numerical extraction. The population-statistics comparison also requires a learning-rate reduction and an initial zero-learning-rate period, so the training recipes differ.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results for V1–V5. No separate numerical rows were extracted from spectra shown only in figures; retained figure-only rows record the text's stated comparisons. Validation accuracies, spectrum-estimator validation, and results cited from prior work were left out because they do not measure the behavior named in the tested version or are not this study's own findings.

untested.parts: Training classification error across model sizes, label corruption, training duration, and regularization. General statements about attaining zero loss are not reported experimental comparisons.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima, and extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation across depths and its prevention by identity shortcuts; special initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Activation-matched initialization, learning speed, and trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, divergence boundaries, and sharpness tracking the stability threshold.

Direct accuracy-gain and learning-rate comparisons between otherwise matched BN and no-BN networks; the specified MNIST and Inception comparisons; Fixup. The direct speed experiment measures training loss rather than accuracy.

missing.what: Inception V3 with population normalization statistics could not be trained without a tiny learning rate of 10^-6. Record the architecture, statistics procedure, and stated restriction without inventing a matched baseline rate or dataset.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for the listed versions. Spectral changes do not justify supporting V6, and an incomplete top-eigenvalue explanation does not challenge V6. No direct BN-versus-no-BN training-speed verdict is warranted from the supplied rows.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and the effects of model size or training duration.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization and spurious minima.
Plain versus residual network training error across depth; special initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Initialization schemes, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
Training behavior above a stability limit and sharpness trajectories relative to that threshold.

Accuracy gain rates and tolerated learning rates are not separately measured for the BN ablations. Comparisons concern CIFAR-10 ResNet-32, VGG CIFAR-10, and ResNet-18 ImageNet spectra, plus optimization speed for a ResNet-32 trained with population versus minibatch BN statistics; they do not test the version's MNIST, Inception, or Santurkar comparisons.

rows.subject: Resnet-32
rows.operation_detail: Ablated batch normalization and compared Hessian spectrum with BN present.
rows.measure: Hessian eigenvalue density, normalized by the respective 10th largest eigenvalue; BN model's eigenvalues contract toward the bulk relative to no-BN model.
rows.value: without BN: outliers grow much larger and further from the bulk
rows.note: The comparison concerns Hessian spectrum, a proposed mechanism associated with training speed, not a direct measurement of accuracy gain rate.
rows.check: Hessian outlier suppression does not measure faster training or higher tolerated learning rates.

rows.subject: VGG network
rows.operation_detail: Compared Hessian spectrum with BN present and after BN removal.
rows.measure: Hessian eigenvalue spectrum; BN suppresses large outliers relative to the network without BN.
rows.value: without BN: outliers grow much larger and further from the bulk
rows.note: This is evidence about the proposed spectral mechanism, not a direct measure of speed.
rows.check: Hessian spectra do not establish V6. Specify modified VGG-11; BN was added to the originally non-BN architecture rather than simply removed.

rows.subject: Resnet-18
rows.operation_detail: Compared Hessian spectrum with BN present and after BN removal.
rows.measure: Hessian eigenvalue spectrum; BN model's largest eigenvalue deviates less from the bulk than the non-BN model.
rows.value: without BN: outliers grow much larger and further from the bulk
rows.note: The text says the same BN-ablation result was obtained on Resnet-18 ImageNet; exact values are figure-only.
rows.check: End-of-training Hessian spectra do not measure training speed or learning-rate tolerance.

rows.subject: Resnet-32
rows.operation_detail: Tracked the ratio of the largest Hessian eigenvalue to the Kth eigenvalue with BN removed versus present.
rows.measure: Relative outlier measure ζ(t); non-BN model consistently shows significantly higher eigenvalue fraction.
rows.value: without BN: consistently significantly higher eigenvalue fraction
rows.note: The reported metric supports outlier suppression as a BN-associated effect, rather than directly quantifying training speed.
rows.check: The eigenvalue ratio measures spectral separation, not the training advantage named in V6.

rows.subject: Resnet-32
rows.operation_detail: Compared covariance spectrum of stochastic gradients with BN versus without BN.
rows.measure: Gradient covariance eigenvalue distribution; without BN almost 99% of the energy is in the top few subspaces.
rows.baseline: with BN: distributions normalized to have the same mean; gradient concentration subsides substantially
rows.value: without BN: almost 99% of energy in top few subspaces
rows.note: The text explicitly describes the non-BN concentration and says it subsides substantially with BN; no exact BN percentage is stated.
rows.check: Gradient concentration is a proposed mechanism, not a direct measurement of V6. The matrix is an uncentered gradient second moment, not a centered covariance.

rows.subject: Resnet-32
rows.operation_detail: Measured gradient energy projected onto the ten dominant Hessian eigenvectors with and without BN.
rows.measure: Fraction of gradient variance in projected subspace; almost all variance in the non-BN model's gradient is in that subspace, and concentration is less in BN networks.
rows.baseline: BN network: gradient less concentrated in high-curvature directions
rows.value: non-BN model: almost all gradient variance in the 10-dimensional subspace
rows.note: Reported as a mechanism associated with optimization, not a direct speed or accuracy measure.
rows.check: The plotted quantity is the fraction of squared full-gradient norm projected onto ten Hessian eigenvectors, not gradient variance. It does not directly measure V6.

rows.subject: Resnet-32
rows.operation_detail: Compared training progress using mini-batch BN statistics with population (full-batch) BN statistics.

conditions.value: population-statistics run uses learning rate divided by 100 and at least 400 initial steps at learning rate 0

rows.measure: Optimization progress in terms of loss; population-statistics BN trains much more slowly than mini-batch BN.
rows.note: Direct speed comparison, but uses a deliberately different BN statistics procedure and adjusted recipe; no numerical loss values are stated in the supplied text.
rows.check: Retain as a procedure-dependent training-speed result. Both networks use normalization; this is not a BN-versus-no-BN comparison. Population statistics require a 100-fold learning-rate reduction and at least 400 initial zero-rate steps, confounding an isolated comparison of convergence speed.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine; versions=[none]. Population-statistics normalization trains much more slowly than mini-batch normalization; both conditions retain normalization. This comparison does not measure V6's advantage from adding BN over a network without it.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2; Appendix F, Resnet-32; Appendix G; Figure 19 caption.
source_check.problem: The reported comparison is accurate, but it cannot establish that V6's BN-versus-no-BN effect is partial.

rows.subject: Resnet-32
rows.operation_detail: Compared Hessian spectra of mini-batch-BN and population-statistics-BN networks.
rows.measure: Hessian spectrum; strong outliers are present with population statistics, while the largest Hessian eigenvalue is roughly the same in both models throughout training.
rows.baseline: mini-batch BN: outliers suppressed into the bulk
rows.value: population-statistics BN: strong outliers persist; largest eigenvalue roughly the same
rows.note: The authors state that the population-statistics model trains much more slowly despite roughly the same largest eigenvalue; the spectrum plot itself has no extracted numeric values.
rows.check: The spectral comparison cannot establish V6 independently. The direct speed result belongs in R7; similar largest eigenvalues challenge a proposed explanation, not V6 itself.

relationships.condition: ResNet-32 on CIFAR-10 using population rather than mini-batch normalization statistics
relationships.reason: R7 reports much slower loss optimization with population statistics, requiring a 100-fold learning-rate reduction and initialization warmup; the training advantage depends on the normalization procedure.
relationships.display_finding: Population statistics slowed loss optimization substantially and required a 100-fold learning-rate reduction plus initialization warmup.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: ResNet-32 on CIFAR-10 using population rather than mini-batch normalization statistics
source_check.reason: R7 compares two normalization procedures, not adding BN versus omitting it. Slower population-statistics training does not establish incomplete or failed BN benefit relative to no normalization.

relationships.condition: Inception V3 using population normalization statistics
relationships.reason: Appendix G explicitly reports inability to train this variant without a learning rate of 10^-6; this text-only result is missing from the rows and qualifies learning-rate tolerance by normalization procedure.
relationships.display_finding: Inception V3 could train with population normalization statistics only at a learning rate of 10^-6.

source_check.condition: Inception V3 using population normalization statistics
source_check.reason: Appendix G states the 10^-6 learning-rate requirement, but gives no corresponding no-BN comparison. This cannot determine V6's relative learning-rate tolerance.

relation.reason: The study investigates an explanation for BN's established optimization benefit without directly testing V6's accuracy-speed or learning-rate advantage over networks without BN.

tranche.reason: The study tests a proposed mechanism using spectra and a normalization-statistics intervention. Its BN-versus-no-BN comparisons measure spectra and gradient geometry; its direct loss-speed comparison retains normalization in both conditions. Neither measures the effect specified by V6.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v1, dated 29 January 2019. The proposed outlier-suppression mechanism and population-statistics slowdown are supported; the ResNet-110 refresh-frequency claim is absent.

statements.correction: ResNet-32, CIFAR-10: population statistics produce much slower loss optimization than mini-batch statistics; learning rate divided by 100; at least 400 initial steps with learning rate 0. Inception V3: population-statistics training required learning rate 10^-6. ResNet-110 alternating-statistics result: not stated.
statements.problem: The ResNet-32 and Inception V3 results are stated. No ResNet-110 alternating-statistics experiment or associated maximum learning rate of 0.01 appears. These normalization-versus-normalization comparisons also do not establish a limitation of V6's BN-versus-no-BN effect.

statements.correction: ResNet-32, CIFAR-10: population statistics produce much slower loss optimization than mini-batch statistics; learning rate divided by 100; at least 400 initial steps with learning rate 0. Both conditions retain normalization. Alternating statistic refresh: not reported.
statements.problem: The population-statistics result is supported, but the claimed ResNet-110 statistic-refresh comparison is absent.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: BN versus no-BN spectral comparisons and the mini-batch versus population-statistics intervention
reader_labels.reason: The study reports BN-associated suppression of Hessian and gradient outliers and slower optimization with population statistics; this supports a BN-linked training advantage in the tested CIFAR-10 and ImageNet settings (R1–R8).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Population-statistics BN compared with mini-batch BN
reader_labels.reason: The population-statistics network trains much more slowly even though its largest Hessian eigenvalue is roughly the same, so the account based on the top eigenvalue alone is incomplete (R7, R8).
